planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring once frost danger has passed, in full sun and well-drained soil; in zone 9 gardens site against a south-facing wall or plan to protect the trunk during hard freezes.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, slightly acidic soil, and protect young trees from hard freezes since this citrus is less cold-hardy than satsuma or kumquat. Sanbokan is a traditional Japanese citrus long grown around Wakayama Prefecture, believed to be a natural hybrid with pomelo-type ancestry; it bears large, thick-rinded, pale yellow-orange fruit with a mild, only lightly acidic flavor that sits between an orange and a grapefruit. Fruit ripens in winter but is typically picked and cured in a cool, dry spot for a few weeks before eating, which softens the rind and mellows any lingering bitterness. Feed lightly with a citrus fertilizer through the growing season, keep soil evenly moist but never waterlogged, and thin heavy fruit sets to encourage larger, better-flavored fruit the following year.
